sections.h2: Who sends a Tallahassee homeowner the tax bill?
sections.html:
The Leon County Tax Collector mails it, using a roll the Leon County Property Appraiser builds. A Tallahassee notice stacks the city's levy on top of county and other lines, and each body picks its own millage. Nothing about the city line is separate paperwork for the owner.

Per the collector, the appraiser multiplies values by the millage rates, then certifies the finished roll for printing. Corrections to a name, mailing address or location go to the appraiser. Escrow customers should have the lender request the original notice from the collector; you get a duplicate.

sections.h2: What millage does the City of Tallahassee levy?
sections.html:
The city's budget book lists 4.4072 mills as adopted for fiscal year 2026, within the 10.0 mill ceiling Florida allows a city. A mill means one dollar for every thousand of taxable value, and the figure it multiplies is the taxable value on the appraiser's record. County, school board and other lines come on top.

Tallahassee has an odd tax base. By the city's own count, government entities own over half the real property within city limits, which pays nothing, since the capital city also hosts two major universities, a community college and a vocational college. To make up for fire protection on those parcels, the city bills a non-ad valorem fire assessment, mostly through the monthly utility statement.

  • Homes pay the fire assessment per dwelling unit.
  • Commercial and other non-residential parcels pay by square footage tier.
  • Electricity sales in the city carry a 10% public service tax, leaving out the fuel adjustment charge.

The appraiser sends the city a preliminary value estimate in June and a final one in July, certified July 1. Two public budget hearings follow in September.

sections.h2: When do Leon County tax bills arrive and fall due?
sections.html:
Bills start going out on November 1 and the tax must be paid before April 1. On April 1 the collector adds a delinquency fee, an advertising fee and interest at 1.5 percent a month, plus statutory collection costs. A list of delinquent owners must be advertised locally within 45 days.

November4%

Before any bill exists, the August TRIM notice shows proposed taxes, and for city property it carries an estimate drawn from the city budget.

sections.h2: What does a Tallahassee homestead exemption cover?
sections.html:
For tax year 2026 the Leon County Property Appraiser quotes up to $51,411 off assessed value. Its first $25,000 reaches every tax, school included. A second slice of up to $26,411 sits on value over $50,000 and skips school taxes. Amendment 5, passed in 2024, indexes that second slice to the CPI.

Ownership and permanent residence on January 1 are required, March 1 is the filing deadline, and nothing happens automatically. The appraiser's office estimates savings around $800 a year.

  • After the first qualifying year, a Save Our Homes cap holds yearly assessed growth to 3% or the CPI change, whichever is smaller.
  • A sale restores the home to just value on the next January 1.
  • An owner who moves can carry part of the saved difference to the next Florida homestead within three years, filing DR-501T.

sections.h2: What city rules and charges meet a Tallahassee seller?
sections.html:
Permits and utility accounts are the city-level items. The city's budget says a building permit is needed for construction, additions, alterations or repairs when labor and materials run over $1,000, residential or commercial. If you did work yourself or hired a handyman, look up the permit history before listing, then ask the city's permit staff how to close anything left open.

The city also bills electric, gas, water, sewer, stormwater and trash, so schedule final readings around closing. Single-family service, which covers properties of up to six units, includes weekly curbside pickup with a 96-gallon garbage cart and a 64-gallon recycling cart, and curbside trash and bulk waste every second week.

  • Stormwater charges follow an equivalent residential unit.
  • Rates for electric, gas, water, sewer and stormwater rise each October 1 with the CPI under the city code.
  • Fire assessments appear on utility bills for most city customers.

sections.h2: How are taxes settled when a Tallahassee house sells?
sections.html:
Your closing agent prorates this year's bill and clears older unpaid years from your proceeds. Phone the collector for a payoff on any delinquent year, because interest runs every month after April 1. Unpaid accounts go to a certificate sale by June 1, and a certificate holder may seek a tax deed once two years have passed.

The deed carries Florida's stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, recorded through the clerk, with every party to the document answerable. Buyers see a different number from yours: after a sale, the property goes back to market value on the following January 1.

sections.h2: What are the choices for a Tallahassee house with tax owed?
sections.html:
List it, sell to a cash buyer, or catch up the tax first. The lien stays with the parcel, so it has to be cleared by closing in every case. For a rental or inherited home with several unpaid years, obtain a payoff letter first so the net figure on any offer is real.

Rentals and inherited homes also raise a utility question: confirm who holds the city accounts and whether any city charges are past due. A cash buyer who accepts the house as is can close without showings or repairs, which helps when you need to settle a tax balance from the price.

faqs.q: What city millage applies to Tallahassee property?
faqs.a: The city's budget lists 4.4072 mills adopted for fiscal year 2026. County, school and other levies add to it on the Leon County bill.

faqs.q: By what date must Leon County tax be paid?
faqs.a: Before April 1. Bills begin going out November 1, and a late bill picks up a delinquency fee, an advertising fee and 1.5 percent interest per month.

faqs.q: How much can I save by paying a Leon County bill early?
faqs.a: Four percent in November, three in December, two in January and one in February, as the Leon County Tax Collector prints it.

faqs.q: How large is the 2026 homestead exemption in Leon County?
faqs.a: Up to $51,411, according to the Leon County Property Appraiser. The first $25,000 touches all taxes; the rest touches non-school taxes above $50,000. Filing closes March 1.

faqs.q: Why does so much Tallahassee property pay no tax?
faqs.a: Governments own over half the real property inside city limits, and it is exempt. The city bills a fire assessment and moves money from its utilities to cover services on those parcels.
